{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVAV-ec8AAAABZvNHNA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BmJKvzhDVHUE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BmJKv", "number": 34, "title": "Make four-view consistency non-blocking by default and simplify contextual settings visibility", "body": "## Problem

A generated text-to-3D project produces four views, then the **consistency inspection can halt generation when those views disagree**. Current new-project defaults are `enabled: true, onFailure: 'stop'` in `src/reference-set.js`. Changing this requires leaving the studio, opening **Workflow editor → Review & execution settings**, and understanding two separate technical settings (**Consistency inspection**, **Inconsistent views**). This is unexpectedly disruptive and hard to discover.

The studio also has a broader layout problem: after previous simplification efforts (#28, #32), **too many useful, everyday controls were hidden together with genuinely advanced options**. Repeatedly opening sections or navigating into another editor adds complexity. Simplicity is not synonymous with hiding every option.

## Expected outcome

### 1. Four-view contradictions warn but do not stop by default

- For **new projects and new default presets**, keep the optional consistency check **enabled** but default its *response to detected contradictions* to **warn and continue** (`onFailure: 'continue'`). Do not silently disable the inspection itself: retain its report/issues and make them available near the generated four-view/preparation result without interrupting normal modeling.
- Let the user choose a single concise **Four-view check** policy:
  - **Off** — skip optional consistency inspection
  - **Warn and continue** — inspect; report contradictions, keep generating (**default**)
  - **Stop on issues** — inspect; stop modeling on contradictions when explicitly selected
- The three choices must map to existing `consistencySettings.enabled` and `onFailure` semantics; do not introduce a contradictory independent boolean. The saved choice must apply to future runs. An explicit consistency-node setting in the Workflow editor still overrides the project default, and the interface must not misrepresent the effective behavior when an override exists.
- **Only subjective cross-view contradictions** should be allowed to continue under Warn and continue. Keep hard errors hard: missing/wrong/duplicate required views, invalid structure/metadata, inspection execution/parsing failure, source violations, blocked asset permissions, protected-base preservation failures and other genuinely invalid inputs must still stop. Never fabricate a passing report.
- Preserve prior run snapshots/records, explicit user choices on existing projects, human-review gates, immutable checkpoints, lineage and export validation. **Do not retroactively restart or auto-approve** a run already stopped/waiting under its captured settings. No broad compatibility/migration work is needed for unsupported old gen3d project formats.

### 2. Put useful settings where the work happens

- Make **Four-view check** discoverable from the **Model studio**, near the input/preparation/four-view controls it affects. A compact single-choice control is sufficient; the user should **not** need to navigate to the Workflow editor and expand a large settings group to change it. Avoid long help text or secondary labels for its ordinary states.
- Prefer showing a small number of **frequently changed, relevant controls directly** rather than burying them in nested `<details>` sections, multiple dialogs or distant editor pages. Equally, do not show irrelevant settings everywhere: use the current task/input mode to decide what belongs on the surface. In image-only flows without generated four views, avoid suggesting this policy will generate/check four new views.
- Audit the current main studio and Workflow editor for **unnecessary multi-level hiding**. Keep ordinary, actionable controls visible at their point of use; leave graph internals, exact hashes, technical feature exceptions and rarely used debugging settings on demand. Do not merely expand all advanced forms or add a new "Advanced" maze.
- Visually communicate layout and meaning using proximity, grouped controls, short labels and state. Keep the interactive 3D viewer dominant; do not reintroduce explanatory paragraphs, verbose secondary labels, redundant confirmations or extra required screens.
- For a contradiction that was allowed, show a **compact non-blocking warning**, with one way to inspect details and the relevant four views. Keep keyboard and screen-reader accessibility, clear focus, Light/Dark parity and narrow-width usability.

### 3. Respect model generation and workflow semantics

- Text still generates the concept and all four required views before modeling; skipping the consistency inspection is **not** permission to skip reference generation.
- Existing explicit Stop policies (project or node), optional manual reviews and failed real validation remain authoritative.
- Use the same persisted effective policy for browser UI, local workflow execution and MCP callers; prevent silently changing permission rules or bypassing human-only approvals.
- Changing the policy for a future run must produce the correct graph/node configuration fingerprint and invalidate only genuinely affected downstream checkpoints; no stale reuse under a mismatched policy.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A brand-new Text → 3D project defaults to checking four-view consistency with **Warn and continue**, not stopping merely because an otherwise valid inspection report identifies contradictions. The report and generated images remain available.
- [ ] From the Model studio, users can choose **Off / Warn and continue / Stop on issues** via one compact, relevant control without entering the Workflow editor. Selection persists on the project and updates future run behavior.
- [ ] Explicit **Stop on issues** blocks a contradictory result; **Off** skips optional inspection; **Warn and continue** retains warning evidence and continues to modeling. Inspect execution/errors or malformed/incomplete four-view evidence still block under every relevant policy.
- [ ] Existing projects with an explicitly saved policy keep that policy; existing run snapshots/pending approvals are not rewritten or auto-continued. Per-node graph overrides still work and the main UI truthfully indicates when the displayed effective policy differs from the project setting.
- [ ] At least the four-view controls and closely related ordinary studio options are audited for unnecessary nested hiding/navigation; main-studio layout remains visual-first and free of additional explanatory clutter. Image-only flows do not offer a misleading four-view action.
- [ ] Consistency settings and warnings behave correctly across built-in presets, saved/edited workflows, checkpoint reuse/branching, Web UI and MCP-driven runs without bypassing permissions, approvals or preservation checks.
- [ ] Browser tests cover new default, all three choices, persistence/reload, allowed warnings vs hard blockers, node override, review gates and relevant text/image context; desktop/narrow Light/Dark layouts, keyboard and accessible names are verified. Record actual screenshots for the relevant studio state(s).
- [ ] Run `npm test`, `npm run check`, and applicable `npm run test:browser` checks, report actual outcomes, skipped checks and the distinction between injected providers and real Codex/Blender runs. Update README/usage docs concisely without a wall of new explanatory text.

## Post-merge verification

None.

## Optional validation

- Brief local first-use walkthrough to check that a user can find and change the policy at the point of use without instructions.
- Real Codex + Blender trial with intentionally contradictory generated views when available; do not spend allowance or require subjective human approval as a mandatory gate for this UI/default change.

## Context

- #28 — visual-first simplified studio and no default intermediate approvals.
- #32 — remove internal jargon and redundant UI copy; this Issue also corrects **over-hiding** ordinary controls.
- Current `main` `e03331943486`:
  - `src/reference-set.js`: `consistencySettings(..., previous = { enabled: true, onFailure: 'stop' })`.
  - `src/workflow.js`: per-node consistency settings override project run snapshot; custom graphs and branching remain supported.
  - `web/index.html`: current consistency policy split across **Consistency inspection** and **Inconsistent views**, inside collapsed **Workflow editor → Review & execution settings**.
  - `web/app.js`: `settings` form patches both policy fields; only shows them in the workflow view.

**Principle:** don't hide controls simply to make the UI look sparse. Show the small set of decisions people actually need at the moment they need them, and let the layout speak instead of compensating with more explanation.
